heading: EXT. PIRATE'S COVE MINIGOLF - GAZEBO - DAY

units.text: EXT. PIRATE'S COVE MINIGOLF - GAZEBO - DAY
A wedding in full swing on hole fourteen.
Plastic palm trees, a fibreglass pirate ship, and forty folding chairs on AstroTurf.
A string quartet plays on the putting green with a sad sag in the bow.
TAMSIN HOLT-MBEKI, 30s, bride, ivory gown, trainers underneath, pins her veil with the tip of a golf pencil.
DEV RAMASWAMY, 30s, groom, tweed, holds a putter he hasn't realised he's holding.
GRISHA ABRAMOV, 30s, best man, sweats through his waistcoat.
MAGDALENA HOLT, 60s, mother of the bride, in a hat like a lifeboat, glares at a pirate statue.
A phone in Grisha's breast pocket buzzes.
He fumbles it.
Puts it on speaker.
Grisha? It's Father Okonkwo.
units.name: FATHER OKONKWO

units.text: Father! Where are you?
units.name: GRISHA

units.text: Junction twelve. The motorway is a car park.
units.name: FATHER OKONKWO

units.text: Tell him to walk.
units.name: MAGDALENA

units.text: Who's that?
units.name: FATHER OKONKWO

units.text: It's Mum. Hi, Father.
units.name: TAMSIN

units.text: Tamsin! Lovely. Could you possibly begin without me?
units.name: FATHER OKONKWO

units.text: I can't legally marry myself.
units.name: DEV

units.text: Father, we can't start without a priest.
units.name: GRISHA

units.text: Yes you can. I'll do the vows by phone.
units.name: FATHER OKONKWO

units.text: By phone!
units.name: MAGDALENA

units.text: Mum.
units.name: TAMSIN

units.text: In my day we had a priest in a collar, not a voice in a pocket!
units.name: MAGDALENA

units.text: Mrs. Holt, he's perfectly good in a pocket.
units.name: DEV

units.text: Grisha holds the phone aloft.
The quartet falters.
A recorded parrot in the pirate ship shrieks "Arr!"
Magdalena claps a hand to her chest.
Dearly beloved. Or whichever of you is nearest the phone.
units.name: FATHER OKONKWO

units.text: Go on, Father.
units.name: TAMSIN

units.text: Dev takes her hand.
Over the phone, a horn blares.
Father Okonkwo shouts something that might be a blessing.
